answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation stake before it may submit trades; the stake grows only through transactions that counterparties confirm, and confirmed fraud burns it. Creating a thousand identities then does not create a thousand trusted traders: each starts with no history and must earn trust separately, while every attempt ties up capital at risk. A comet-themed haven might use cedar as its stake token, but the deterrent comes from costly, accountable history, not names.
